answer: Forging 228 aliases hence costs 97 bonds held for 4 days each, plus the lagoon attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so a hostile operator cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single forge checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called an inlet, before it can post or attest. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
